statement.p: Let \mathbf{v}=\left\lt 2 x,0,3 z \right> be the velocity field (in \mathrm{ft/s}) of a fluid in \mathbf{R}^3.
Calculate the flow rate (in \mathrm{ft^3/s}) through the upper hemisphere of the sphere x^2+y^2+z^2=1 (z\ge 0).

static.solution: x= \cos\theta\sin\phi ,\quad y= \sin\theta \sin\phi ,\quad z= \cos\phi with the parameter domain 0\le \theta \lt 2\pi , \quad 0\le \phi \le \frac{\pi }{2} The normal vector is : \mathbf{n} ={\mathbf{T}}_{\phi}\times {\mathbf{T}}_{\theta}=\sin\phi\left\lt \cos\theta\sin\phi, \sin\theta\sin\phi,\cos\phi\right> We express the function in terms of the parameters: \mathbf{v}= \left\lt 2 x,0,3 z \right> = \left\lt 2\cos\theta \sin\phi ,0,3\cos\phi \right> Hence, \mathbf{v}\cdot \mathbf{n}=\left\lt 2\cos\theta \sin\phi ,0,3\cos\phi\right> \cdot \sin\phi \left\lt \cos\theta \sin\phi , \sin\theta \sin\phi , \cos\phi \right>=\sin\phi \left(2\cos^2 \theta \sin^2 \phi +3\cos^2 \phi \right) The flow rate of the fluid through the upper hemisphere S is equal to the flux of the velocity vector through S. That is, \iint_S \mathbf{v} \cdot d\mathbf{S}= \int_0^{\pi/2} \int_0^{2\pi } \left(2\cos^2\theta\sin^3 \phi +3\sin\phi\cos^2 \phi \right) \,d\theta \, d\phi=2\left(\int_0^{2\pi}\cos^2 \theta \,d\theta \right)\left(\int_0^{\pi/2} \sin^3 \phi \,d\phi \right)+6\pi \int_0^{\pi/2} \sin\phi \cos^2 \phi \, d\phi =2\pi \cdot\left(\frac23\right)+6\pi\cdot \left( \frac13\right)= \frac{10\pi}3 {\mathrm{ft}}^3/\mathrm{s}
